Definition: complete; as noun, the whole (specifically, a sacrifice entirely consumed); as adverb, fully
BiblicalUsage: Kaliyl is the whole — complete, entire, and as a noun the whole burnt offering, the sacrifice consumed entirely on the altar. Every meat offering for the priest shall be wholly burnt; Moses says Levi shall put whole burnt sacrifice upon God's altar; and Samuel offered a sucking lamb for a burnt offering wholly unto the LORD.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the whole burnt offering is the picture of a whole life given. Nothing was kept back, nothing eaten, nothing sold — it all went up to God, and that is what I hold consecration to mean.
